The $3.72 FY27 consensus remains paywalled and unverified, so I use ~$3.97 (midpoint). I keep 28x (four of five agents); agent_1's extra turn is not backed by new evidence. The stock is ~32x the current NTM EPS (~$3.45), so 28x a year out already assumes ~4 turns of de-rating as growth slows to mid-teens.
disagreements.evidence: Rambus Q1/Q2 2026 8-K Ex.99.1; stockanalysis.com forecast page (2027 paywalled).

disagreements.positions: All five now deduct ~$50M/yr; my round-1 file said ~$100M/yr.
disagreements.resolution: Deduct, but size it from the filings. Payments of taxes on net share settlement: $52.7M H1-2026 (10-Q), vs $35.0M H1-2025 and $41.9M FY2025 (10-K XBRL), so ~84% falls in H1 with Q1 vesting. 2026 should be ~$55-62M, not ~$100M (my round-1 error) and a little above the agents' $50M; it scales with the share price. It is the cash cost of SBC (FY2025 SBC $54.3M) that non-GAAP EPS excludes, so deducting it from FCF is correct and not a double count with dilution as long as share count is held flat.
disagreements.evidence: Rambus 10-Q Q2 2026 cash-flow statement; SEC XBRL companyfacts (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation 2021-2025).

disagreements.topic: Adding net cash on top of interest-inclusive earnings or FCF (agent_4's point)
disagreements.positions: agent_4: adding cash to a P/E on EPS that includes interest income double counts; agents 1, 3, 4, 5 still add $0.75-0.78B of net cash to an FCF-yield value.
disagreements.resolution: agent_4 is right, and the same logic applies to the FCF legs. H1-2026 'interest income and other income, net' was $14.2M (~$28M/yr pre-tax, ~$24M after a 16% tax), about $0.22/share. In a 28x P/E that is worth ~$6/share, close to the ~$7/share of cash, so P/E without a cash add is about right. In a 3.0% FCF yield the interest is capitalized at ~$0.8B (~$7.3/share), so adding the $0.76B of cash on top double counts ~$7/share (~$6 at 3.5%). Correct method: strip interest from FCF, then add cash.
disagreements.evidence: Rambus 10-Q Q2 2026 income statement and 'Interest and Other Income' discussion.
